sources.entry: Markup - Reader-first, native macOS Markdown editor: renders notes like a web page and edits on demand, with a vault, backlinks, graph view and full-text search.

summary.one_liner: Markup is a free, open-source, native macOS Markdown editor that renders notes as a web-style reading view and switches to WYSIWYG or raw-source editing on demand.
summary.what_it_does: Opens a folder of .md files as a vault with a virtual-scrolled file tree, multiple tabs, and Quick Open (⌘P). Notes render in a read-first view with KaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, syntax-highlighted code, GFM tables and task lists; press E for WYSIWYG editing (Milkdown/ProseMirror) or ⌘/ for CodeMirror 6 source. It provides wikilinks ([[file]] and [[file#heading]]), backlinks, a graph view, and full-text search via Tantivy (⌘⇧F). Notes can be exported or previewed as themed HTML (GitHub, plain, or Tufte themes), with code, math and diagrams preserved, or printed to PDF. The README also lists file watching with reload prompts, auto-save, image paste into an assets folder, light/dark/sepia themes, and English/Chinese UI.
use_cases: Reading and browsing a folder of Markdown notes
Writing and editing Markdown with WYSIWYG or raw source
Building a linked personal knowledge base with backlinks and graph view
Searching across a large set of Markdown files
Exporting notes to shareable HTML or PDF
Writing technical docs with math and Mermaid diagrams
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
notable: Reader-first design: notes render as a web page by default, with editing on demand
Tauri-based native app using the system WebView, reported at about 88 MB idle RAM
Tantivy-powered full-text search, with the README citing a 10,000-file vault indexing in about 1 second
One-click HTML export that keeps syntax highlighting, KaTeX math and Mermaid diagrams, with a self-contained file for ordinary docs
Signed and notarized macOS DMG builds for Apple Silicon and Intel
caveats: macOS only, and the README describes it as pre-1.0
Building from source requires macOS 12+, Node 18+, pnpm 8+, Rust 1.77+ and Xcode Command Line Tools; the first build takes 5–10 minutes
Exports of documents with math or diagrams load those renderers from a CDN
